To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cone horizontal cell axon synapses in the goldfish inner nuclear layer are primarily onto bipolar cells.

horizontal cell axon synaptic terminals in the inner nuclear layer of the goldfish retina make both excitatory and inhibitory synaptic contacts with bipolar cell dendrites, axons and perikarya, and that they also make synaptic contacts with interplexiform cell perikarya and dendrites.
cone horizontal cell axon synapses in the goldfish inner nuclear layer form typical chemical synapses and contribute to antagonistic surrounds in bipolar cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the morphology of synaptic connections of the cone horizontal cell axon in the goldfish.
the functional organization of the retina, with a particular emphasis on horizontal cell function and the synaptic interactions between horizontal cells and other neurons.
the functional role of the horizontal cell axons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the horizontal cell system in the goldfish is a complex and multifunctional one.

horizontal cell axon synapses in the inner nuclear layer are not only involved in the horizontal cell feedback circuit but also contribute to the antagonism of bipolar cell responses and the modulation of interplexiform cell input to the outer p lexiform layer.

horizontal cell axons are the major output pathway of the cone horizontal cell network in goldfish retina, and that they contribute to the antagonism of the bipolar cell receptive fields and modulate inputs to interplexiform cells and the outer plexifom layer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the horizontal cell processes in the goldfish are not only involved in horizontal interactions, but also in interactions among different types of retinal neurons.
cone horizontal cell axon terminal synapses in the goldfish are not restricted to the inner plexiform layer, but also form synapses in the middle of inner nuclear layer.
cone horizontal cells in fish retina are not only the major output neurons of the inner plexiform layer but they are also the major input neurons of the outer plexform layer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cone horizontal cells are not simply passive elements in retinal circuits, but they actively modulate synaptic transmission at the level of the inner nuclear and outer plexiform layers.

the horizontal cells of goldfish retina are not only the major input to the outer pexiform layer of the retina but also provide an output to bipolar cells and interplexiform cells in the inner nuclear layer of the retina.
horizontal cell axon synapses are not only input synapses but also output synapses.
